newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Kmart busy, stock rallies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Kmart busy, stock rallies.

text.p: Kmart Corp, which is slated to report first quarter earnings Thursday, rallied on expectations of a positive surprise, traders said Wednesday.

Both the underlying stock and the options were busy as the retailer's stock climbed through the key 14 level. In late trade, the stock was up 5/8 at 14-3/8, just below its 14-5/8 session peak, which represented a new 52-week high.
"We're hearing earnings are going to be better than expected," said John Burnside, a market maker in Kmart options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
Last week, the company said it expected to report a first quarter profit, which would reverse a $0.08 per share loss from continuing operations reported in last year's first quarter.
Analysts' consensus estimate is for a profit of $0.01 per share, but traders said the "whisper" estimate on Wall Street is for earnings of up to $0.05 a share.
"The rumor on the Street is it could be as high as a nickel," Burnside said.
A couple analysts said they would be surprised if Kmart posted a $0.05 per share profit.
"It's the first time the stock has been acting well in quite some time," Burnside said. "It's broken some serious resistance and we're thinking it might go higher."
Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at Everen Securities, said the 14 level was a key breakdown point in late 1995 and was proved to be stiff resistance on the mid-1996 rebound.
"You're trying to get through previous resistance, which speaks bullishly for the intermediate term," he said. "But you still face old resistance from the previous decline in the 15 to 16 area."
